author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty

the page carries the navigation every page carries, and no page links to it
all page wording comes from the message bundles and is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002)

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package, which already owns Vet, Specialty and the vet directory page (system-design.md#package-structure). Three things are new ground rather than a repeat of an existing pattern, which is why the verdict is new rather than minor. First, Specialty gains its own repository: SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow org.springframework.data.repository.Repository like VetRepository, exposing one name-ordered read and no write method, which keeps NG-2 enforced by the type's surface rather than by convention. It deliberately does not follow PetTypeRepository, which extends JpaRepository and so exposes a full CRUD surface. Second, the inverse view of the vet-to-specialty association is derived in memory by a new value object, SpecialtyDirectory, instead of by an inverse @ManyToMany on Specialty - recorded in ADR 2026-08-15-specialty-directory-derived-in-memory.md, because a bidirectional mapping would make the serialized vet representation on /vets cyclic and would need eager fetch on both sides under the disabled open-session-in-view. Third, the route-level contract the PRD keeps out of its prose is now recorded on the design side: GET /specialties.html, rendering vets/specialtyList through the shared layout fragment with a menu selector that matches no navigation item, so the page carries the navigation without any entry linking to it. The controller stays a Web controller per the pattern catalog: it reads the two collections, delegates the pairing and the ordering to SpecialtyDirectory, and selects the view. No business rule is added to VetController, so the recorded controller-rule deviation is not extended.
integration_points: VetController gains a third GET route, /specialties.html, and a second constructor dependency on SpecialtyRepository; the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) test class therefore needs a second @MockitoBean or the whole test class moves to a real repository
SpecialtyDirectory.of(Collection<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>) is the single pairing and ordering point; the controller and the template hold no grouping logic
VetRepository.findAll() (the cached, unpaged read) supplies the veterinarians; the paged findAll(Pageable) is untouched

The new template renders through fragments/layout.html, so every wording token is a #{} key that must exist in all eleven message bundles - I18nPropertiesSyncTest walks src/main and fails the build on a hard-coded string or a missing key
Vet.getSpecialties() already returns a fresh name-sorted list, so the directory needs no extra sorting on the vet side

patterns.description: narrow Spring Data Repository base exposing only the reads the feature needs - SpecialtyRepository follows this, not PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository
Value object row: SpecialtyDirectory is immutable, defensively copies its collections, and enforces its ordering at construction; the persistence-entity exception does not apply to it
existing precedent for display ordering owned by the model rather than the template
existing directory page: layout fragment, table markup, and the #{none} key already used for a veterinarian holding no specialty

risks.risk: Matching a specialty against Vet.getSpecialties() by object equality silently yields an empty page. BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, the veterinarians come from the @Cacheable("vets") collection loaded in an earlier session, and the specialties come from a fresh read, so the two sides are different instances of the same rows
risks.mitigation: Pair on getId(); cover it with a SpecialtyDirectory unit test that builds the two collections as separate instance graphs rather than sharing one Specialty object

risks.risk: Sorting the collection returned by VetRepository.findAll() in place corrupts the shared cache entry for every later request
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory copies into a new list before ordering and never mutates its inputs

risks.risk: A specialty held by no veterinarian, or a veterinarian holding none, falls out of the page through the wrong join direction
risks.mitigation: Drive the outer iteration from the specialty collection, not from the vets; the two acceptance criteria for these cases are separate tests

risks.risk: Adding a second cached read would widen the unevicted-cache question already open in system-design.md#open-questions-from-the-survey
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository is left uncached; recorded in the ADR's consequences

risks.risk: New wording keys missing from one of the eleven bundles fail I18nPropertiesSyncTest late in the loop
risks.mitigation: Add every new key to all bundles in the same step; reuse the existing #{name}, #{specialties} and #{none} keys where they fit

That file is the product expert's to write; flagged for the next slice that touches vocabulary. || Narrowest-reading choice recorded rather than raised: the page is added to VetController rather than a new SpecialtyController, matching the prd-entry's file_targets. A separate controller becomes the answer if the page later grows the search or filter behavior the entry lists as non-goals. || Ordering source: specialties come back name-ordered from the repository query (the PetTypeRepository precedent), veterinarians are last-name ordered inside SpecialtyDirectory. notes: Records gap closed. Both paths are now in supporting_paths. The audit was correct and the code was never at fault. || Implementer judgment call 1 CONFIRMED. SpecialtyDirectory.of rejecting a specialty with no id is the right call, not merely a defensible one. Objects.equals(null, null) is true, so an unsaved specialty would pair with a veterinarian's unsaved one; guarding the specialty side alone closes the trap, because a non-null specialty id can never match a null held id. Rejecting rather than filtering keeps a data defect loud, and the input comes from the repository, so the throw is unreachable in production. This is invariant enforcement at construction, which architecture-principles requires of every type outside the persistence-entity exception. Now recorded in durable memory: one state sentence under the derived-not-mapped statement in system-design.md#contracts, with the reasoning in the ADR's Consequences. || Implementer judgment call 2 CONFIRMED. Reusing the vets key for the column heading is correct. The key is a vocabulary label, not page-specific text: layout.html already uses it for the navigation entry and vetList.html for its page heading, and all eleven bundles translate it as the plain plural noun. It is the exact mirror of specialties, which vetList uses as a column heading and the new page as its heading. A new key would duplicate one translation across eleven bundles and invite drift. No durable-memory write; the existing pages already demonstrate the pattern. || Correction to my own line-5 record. That record and the ADR called SpecialtyDirectory a value object, which the pattern catalog defines as having equality by value. The type cannot have it: Entry holds Specialty and Vet, persistence entities carrying identity and no value equality, so any equals would be reference-based underneath and would be fake value equality. Reclassified in this dispatch as an immutable per-request projection - one Contracts row in system-design.md, and a Decision paragraph in the ADR stating that it realizes the catalog's other value-object properties (immutability, no identity of its own, construction-time invariants). author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: not verified against the NVD in this review. The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (only cyclonedx-bom 3.2.4 is present), and this reviewer has no network access, so no CVE match ran. The change adds no dependency at all — build.gradle and gradle/ are untouched — so it introduces no new supply-chain surface. For the record, the resolved framework floor is Spring Boot 4.1.0 via the Boot plugin. Closing the NVD check is a human or CI task, not a defect in this slice.

Performance/DoS note (informational, not a finding at this baseline): showSpecialtyDirectory pairs the full specialty and veterinarian tables per request with a nested scan, and SpecialtyRepository.findAll() is uncached while VetRepository.findAll() is cached. Both tables are seed-sized and bounded by stored data rather than by caller input, and the unpaginated /vets route is the existing baseline, so this is not a widening. Worth revisiting only if the clinic data grows.
approved_aspects: XSS: specialtyList.html renders every request-visible value through th:text (entry.specialty.name, vet.firstName/lastName) and the i18n keys through #{...}. No th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no external resource loading, and no request-derived value in Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) — the layout fragment call passes the literal 'specialties'. Default output escaping stays on, matching the control in docs/security-principles.md.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() uses a fixed JPQL string ('SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name') with no parameters and no concatenation. The ORDER BY is a compile-time literal, not caller-supplied, so no sort-column injection path exists.

Least privilege at the repository: SpecialtyRepository extends the bare Repository marker and exposes exactly one read method and no write, so specialties cannot be mutated through the application. This is a narrower surface than the derived-CRUD alternative.

Exposed surface: /specialties.html is a GET with no request parameters, no path variables, and no request body. It exposes specialty names and veterinarian names, both already public on /vets.html and the /vets JSON route, so it discloses nothing beyond the recorded baseline in system-design.md § Security Context. No mass-assignment surface is added (no form, no WebDataBinder).
Path traversal / resource resolution: no request-derived value composes a filesystem or classpath path. The view name 'vets/specialtyList' is a fixed literal.

Shared-state safety: SpecialtyDirectory.of copies the incoming collections before sorting (new ArrayList<>(specialties), holdersOf builds its own list), so the @Cacheable("vets") collection shared across requests is never reordered or mutated. SpecialtyDirectory and Entry are final, hold List.copyOf snapshots, and expose only immutable views — no unsynchronized mutable state reachable from the singleton controller. SpecialtyDirectoryTests.shouldLeaveTheGivenCollectionsInTheOrderTheyArrivedIn pins this.

Error handling: the IllegalArgumentException from requireStoredIdentity carries a specialty name only — no credential, connection string, or identifier beyond data already rendered on the page — and error.html renders ${message} through th:text, so even that value is escaped. The path is also unreachable from the web route, since persisted specialties always carry a generated id.

Resource management: no file handles, streams, executors, regex, XML/JSON/YAML parsing, deserialization, shell execution, or network I/O introduced. No SecureRandom-relevant code. No System.out/System.err and no logging added, so no log-injection or secret-in-log surface.
Secrets: no hardcoded credential, token, key, or connection string in the diff. build.gradle and gradle/ are unchanged.
